headline: Karissa has new evening confusion (reported Nov 15, including a stove left on) after a Sep 23 fall and a Nov 5 ED visit for dehydration and dizziness. The planned workup results are not in the record.

items.statement: On Nov 15, 2026 her son Marcus reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. She was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. No results or PCP visit note are in the evidence.
items.verifier_note: All details match the Nov 15 nursing note. The absence of results or a PCP note is a statement about the evidence, and the cited note doesn't contradict it.

items.statement: Karissa fell in the bathroom at night on Sep 23, 2026, and Marcus found her on the floor. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness, and no injury was noted. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: Every detail matches the Sep 23 nursing note: bathroom fall at night, Marcus found her, no head strike or LOC, no injury, high fall risk, and a PT referral.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on Oct 1, 2026 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: The Oct 1 PT evaluation matches on gait, intermittent cane use, TUG of 19 seconds, the walker, home safety evaluation and grab bars, and PT twice weekly.

items.statement: She was seen in the partner hospital ED on Nov 5, 2026 for dehydration and dizziness, and was treated and released the same day with no new medications. At the Nov 11 PCP follow-up she was back to baseline per her son, and the plan was close monitoring for two weeks. Evening confusion was then reported on Nov 15.
items.verifier_note: The ED summary, the Nov 11 PCP note and the Nov 15 nursing note support every detail. These are the ED visit for dehydration and dizziness with same-day release and no new medications, the return to baseline per her son, monitoring for two weeks, and the later confusion report.

items.statement: The evidence does not show whether the walker, home safety evaluation or bathroom grab bars recommended on Oct 1 were completed. It also shows no PT progress notes after the evaluation.
items.verifier_note: The Oct 1 note recommends the walker, home safety evaluation and grab bars. It says nothing about completion and has no follow-up PT notes, so the statement about missing evidence is accurate.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on Nov 15 completed, and what did they show?
Does the evening confusion relate to the Nov 5 dehydration and dizziness, and what hydration monitoring is in place?
Were the walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars put in place, and how is PT progressing since the Oct 1 evaluation?
What supports are in place for night-time safety and for the stove, given the Sep 23 night fall and the Nov 15 stove incident, and how is Marcus coping?

A withheld note (n013) says the Nov 15 confusion is resolved and removed from the active problem list, but it records no new assessment. Can the team review it and confirm whether the concern should stay active?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and discharges, with reasons.

Falls check: any falls or near-falls in the window, injuries, and whether fall-risk screening or a fall-risk plan was updated. Note that she is 85 and on antiplatelet therapy (clopidogrel) plus a beta-blocker, so bleeding or injury from a fall is relevant.

Cardiac symptom review for ischemic heart disease: chest pain or angina episodes, use of PRN nitroglycerin spray (frequency and dates), dyspnea, palpitations, and any cardiology visits or ECG/testing ordered or completed.

Medication reconciliation: the simvastatin 10 mg entry started 2026-08-16 alongside simvastatin 20 mg (started 2020-07-11) is a possible duplicate or dose conflict. Verify with the prescriber which statin dose is intended, whether one was stopped, and whether the patient is taking both. Also confirm clopidogrel and metoprolol are still active and check for any new starts or stops in the window.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window (metoprolol use), including any orthostatic symptoms, dizziness, or bradycardia flags.
Lipid and glycemic follow-up: check for any lipid panel, A1c or glucose results since the last review, given hyperlipidemia and prediabetes, and whether monitoring is due.
Weight and BMI trend (obesity, BMI 30+), including any unintentional weight loss or gain and nutrition or dietitian referrals.
Cancer history follow-up for breast malignancy (dx 1997): surveillance imaging or oncology visits due or completed, and any new symptoms reported.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, meal preparation, medication management, and mobility aids compared with the last assessment.

Cognition, mood, and social: any cognitive screen changes, depression screen, reported loneliness or distress, caregiver situation and availability, and attendance at PACE center days and therapies. Confirm care-plan items due in the window (reassessments, goals, caregiver check-ins) and list any overdue items for the IDT to discuss.
